description: One statement period on one bank account, and whether the books tie out against it. Opening balance plus everything that moved is what the closing balance SHOULD be; the bank's own closing balance is what it is; the gap between them is the variance and it is the only number on this record that matters. A period-by-period chain of these is the proof that a year of transactions is complete — a missing month shows up as a chain gap, a missing transaction shows up as a variance, and neither is findable from the transaction list alone.
name: Statement Anchor

fields.description: The account this period belongs to. A proper Link rather than a raw Plaid account id, which is what makes an anchor company-scoped, joinable to its Bank Transactions, and exportable with the rest of a company's records.
fields.label: Bank Account

fields.description: Copied from the Bank Account when the anchor is saved, and read-only here. Derived rather than entered, and stored rather than joined: every reconciliation question is asked one company at a time, and a filter that needed a join to the Bank Account would be the join every one of those queries pays for.
fields.label: Company

fields.description: The last four digits the bank prints on the statement. Indexed, because a person asking whether ••6030 tied out in October has the mask and not the docname.
fields.label: Plaid Account Mask

fields.description: Which version of the statement parser produced these numbers. Kept because a variance that appears across every account in one month is a parser change, not a bookkeeping problem, and this is the column that says so.
fields.label: Parser Version

fields.description: The upstream statement id, for tracing a row back to the PDF it was read off. Migration traceability only — nothing here reads it to make a decision.
fields.label: Source Statement ID

fields.description: Opening balance per the statement. In a healthy chain this equals the prior period's closing balance; where it does not, chain_gap_from_prior says so.
fields.label: Anchored Opening

fields.description: Everything that moved in the period. POSITIVE IS MONEY IN — deposits, interest, dividends, sale proceeds — and negative is money out. Same convention as Bank Transaction's signed amount, so no sign is flipped anywhere between the two.
fields.label: Transaction Sum

fields.description: anchored_opening + transaction_sum. What the closing balance would be if every movement in the period were on file.
fields.label: Computed Closing

fields.description: Closing balance per the statement. The bank's number, not ours.
fields.label: Anchored Closing

fields.description: anchored_closing - computed_closing. Positive means the bank has more money than the transactions on file account for, so something that came IN is missing; negative means something that went OUT is missing.
fields.label: Variance

fields.description: How far off a period may be and still count as reconciled. A cent by default, which is rounding. A brokerage account whose advisory fee never appears in the bank feed needs a variance_reason, not a wider tolerance — widening this is how a real missing transaction gets filed as noise.
fields.label: Variance Tolerance

fields.description: Computed on save: abs(variance) is within the tolerance. Read-only, because a period nobody can explain is not reconciled by ticking a box.
fields.label: Reconciled

fields.description: Computed on save: the prior period's closing balance is not this period's opening balance. Usually a statement nobody has loaded yet — a gap in the chain is a MISSING PERIOD, which no amount of per-transaction checking will find.
fields.label: Chain Gap From Prior

fields.description: Why this period does not tie out, in a sentence a person wrote. "Quarterly advisory fee $3,774.81, not in the bank feed" is an explained variance and is worth more than a tolerance wide enough to swallow it, because next quarter's fee will be a different number and the explanation still fits.
fields.label: Variance Reason

fields.description: Total account value including securities, at the start of the period. Empty on a depository account. NOT part of the chain: the anchor reconciles cash and sweep, never market value.
fields.label: Portfolio Opening Value

fields.description: Total account value including securities, at the end of the period. Empty on a depository account.
fields.label: Portfolio Closing Value

fields.description: The part of the portfolio move that no cash movement explains — the market, in other words. Reported beside the cash chain and never added to it, because a position that went up is not money that arrived.
fields.label: Mark To Market Delta

fields.description: The period as the STATEMENT prints it, where a parser has supplied it. Optional, and empty on most anchors: the chain arithmetic above needs only three numbers. What these buy is the one question the numbers cannot answer — WHICH movement is missing — because a line here with no Bank Transaction behind it is a transaction the feed never delivered.
fields.label: Statement Lines

fields.description: The statement PDF, where somebody has attached one. OPTIONAL by design — the pipe that parses statements already stores them, and this app owns the reconciliation truth whether or not it owns the bytes.
fields.label: Statement PDF

fields.description: The anchor this one replaces. A restated period is a new record pointing at the old one rather than an edit, so the number somebody reconciled against last quarter is still readable.
fields.label: Amended From
